CFML Language Reference: Functions

CreateTime

Builds a time-of-day value from three numbers. Because every date/time value also has a date, the date part is the zero date, December 30, 1899.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

CreateTime(hour, minute, second)

Parameters

hour
Hour, 0 to 23.
minute
Minute, 0 to 59.
second
Second, 0 to 59.

Returns

A date/time value. Printed directly it shows the zero date: {ts '1899-12-30 14:30:00'}.

Usage

Display the result with TimeFormat; DateFormat would faithfully show you December 30, 1899, which is rarely what anyone wants. Out-of-range values throw an "Invalid time." error. To combine a date and a time in one value, use CreateDateTime.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Lunch = CreateTime(12, 30, 0)>
<CFSET Quitting = CreateTime(17, 0, 0)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH></TH><TH>Raw value</TH><TH>TimeFormat</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>Lunch</TD><TD>#Lunch#</TD><TD>#TimeFormat(Lunch, "h:mm tt")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Quitting time</TD><TD>#Quitting#</TD><TD>#TimeFormat(Quitting, "h:mm tt")#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P>Afternoon shift: #DateDiff("h", Lunch, Quitting)# hours (and a half).</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
